div.div:
How it works
• The browser sends If-None-Match with the last ETag; the API returns 304 when the job revision and the caller's scope are unchanged.
• Each unchanged poll doubles the interval (2 → 4 → 8 → 15 s cap); any change resets to 2 s; terminal states (ready, failed, blocked, unknown) stop polling.
• Saved results are re-authorized on every read; a scope change withholds them.

display: inline-block; font-size: 15px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#232F3E, #bdc7d4); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Why not push? Jobs finish in seconds and users watch one job at a time; polling with 304s is cheap, works through CloudFront and the ALB unchanged, and has no connection state. Trigger for SSE/WebSockets: many concurrent watchers needing sub-second updates.
